BBC News (Tabby Wilson) — published Friday 25 September 2026 03:51 BST (metadata cXenseParse:publishtime 2026-09-25T02:51:36Z UTC = 03:51 BST)

HEADLINE: Miliband tells Iran minister UK will not tolerate 'hostile activity' on British soil

FACTS:
- Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi that the UK will "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil". The ministers met face-to-face at the UN General Assembly in New York.
- The Foreign Office said Miliband spoke about "the UK's unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups in UK soil, including attacks on the British Jewish community", and discussed the war in the Middle East and a British couple detained in Iran.
- There was no immediate comment from Araghchi. The Islamic Republic News Agency reported the men met and "discussed bilateral ties and international developments during their talks".
- The comments follow an arson attack on four Jewish community ambulances in Golders Green in March and other incidents. The BBC understands British intelligence chiefs initially kept an open mind on whether the Iranian state or organisations working for it had a role in the Hatzola ambulance attack and other attacks on Jewish communities during 2026; they later concluded that secret intelligence pointed to Iran or its proxies being involved.
- In July a small power plant in the UK was shut down due to a cyber attack.
- Miliband told Araghchi Iran should choose "de-escalation and diplomacy instead of prolonging the war" and stressed the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
- Miliband also raised the detention of British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, from East Sussex, held for more than 20 months after being arrested while passing through Iran on a motorcycle journey. In February they were each sentenced to 10 years on espionage charges, which they deny. Miliband reiterated the call for their immediate release.

QUOTE (Ed Miliband, Foreign Secretary, to Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, per the Foreign Office): the UK will "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil".
QUOTE (Foreign Office statement): Miliband stressed "the UK's unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups in UK soil, including attacks on the British Jewish community".
QUOTE (Ed Miliband, per Foreign Office): Iran should choose "de-escalation and diplomacy instead of prolonging the war".
